bonner-springs/0.title: Short-term rental rules
bonner-springs/0.summary: The council worked on zoning rules for short-term rentals, settling on a 1,000-foot spacing requirement and a cap of six in the central area; a modified ordinance needs a two-thirds vote.

bonner-springs/1.title: Water and sewer rate increases
bonner-springs/1.summary: A utility rate study recommended raising the water service charge 14.1% to $28.46 a month and the usage rate 10.9% to $10.28 per 1,000 gallons, with wastewater changes too.

bonner-springs/2.title: Lynn Valley housing incentive district and subdivision
bonner-springs/2.summary: Bonner Springs set up a Reinvestment Housing Incentive District to pay infrastructure for the Lynn Valley subdivision at 13852 Kansas Avenue, rezoned it 7-1 and approved the first plat, with a hearing set for November 9.

bonner-springs/3.title: New subdivisions on the west side (Mission Prairie Farms, Bungalows, Tiner Acres)
bonner-springs/3.summary: The city approved plats and rezonings for Mission Prairie Farms on 118th Street, the Bungalows on 130th Street, Tiner Acres on 134th Street and Carter Acres on 122nd.

bonner-springs/4.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral rate
bonner-springs/4.summary: The council adopted a resolution to exceed the revenue-neutral rate and a $37.6 million 2027 budget, with changes to library funding.

bonner-springs/5.title: RV park on North 134th Street
bonner-springs/5.summary: A special use permit for The Springs RV Park in a rural residential district was continued to November.

bonner-springs/6.title: Downtown Oak Street housing and walkability plan
bonner-springs/6.summary: The city adopted a Connectivity and Walkability Plan, adjusted a state housing grant for 120 on Oak, approved a below-grade apartment at 125 Oak and replats on Oak and Front Streets, as downtown storefronts hit full occupancy.

bonner-springs/7.title: Senior Villas bonds
bonner-springs/7.summary: The council authorized industrial revenue bonds for Bonner Springs Senior Villas.

bonner-springs/8.title: E-bikes and e-scooters
bonner-springs/8.summary: The police chief presented options for regulating e-mobility devices for safety.

bonner-springs/9.title: Centennial Park extension and Center Park shelter
bonner-springs/9.summary: The city approved buying land to extend Centennial Park and an $88,000 shelter at Center Park.

edgerton/0.title: Data center at Logistics Park Kansas City
edgerton/0.summary: Residents from Edgerton and nearby towns filled public comment at meeting after meeting over a data center allowed by right in the logistics park, raising water use, chemical contamination, fuel tanks, power, conflicts of interest and the lack of a public hearing when data centers were added to the zoning code; others defended its economic benefits.
edgerton/0.where: Logistics Park Kansas City (31800 W 196th St area)

edgerton/1.title: DAMAC data center plat and rock crushing at 196th Street
edgerton/1.summary: The planning commission and council handled a final plat with land dedication for DAMAC Digital's "Edgerton Project" data center at 31800 W 196th Street and a temporary rock crushing permit for its construction, after a revised site plan was withdrawn.

edgerton/2.title: Public comment rules, microphones and a lawsuit
edgerton/2.summary: Residents criticized limits on public comment time, asked for microphones so people can hear meetings, and questioned the mayor's role and attorney fees in litigation.

edgerton/3.title: Pavement condition and street maintenance targets
edgerton/3.summary: Consultants and staff presented a pavement management plan rating Edgerton streets at about 86 out of 100 and asked the council to pick a target condition to guide street budgets.

edgerton/4.title: Truck container yard at 32612 W 191st Street
edgerton/4.summary: The council rezoned about 21 acres to logistics park and approved a cargo container storage and maintenance facility for DeLong Trucking.

edgerton/5.title: 2027 budget, senior tax rebates and rising taxes
edgerton/5.summary: The council adopted a 2027 budget at the same mill rate as 2026 and considered raising its senior property tax rebate budget, while residents urged more frugal spending.

edgerton/6.title: Dwyer Farms workforce housing
edgerton/6.summary: The Dwyer Farms housing development, which will grow Edgerton's housing by about 45%, got a concept report and a regional economic development award.

edgerton/7.title: Railroad quiet zone, K-33 waterline and 2027-2031 capital plan
edgerton/7.summary: The council ratified quiet zone rules and awarded construction for the quiet zone project, created a K-33 waterline relocation project and took up the 2027-2031 capital program.

edwardsville/0.title: 2027 budget, revenue-neutral rate and big property tax increases
edwardsville/0.summary: At the revenue-neutral rate hearing, residents described property tax bills rising as much as 31% and said they are protesting appraisals; council discussed what it controls on the tax bill.

edwardsville/1.title: Dust and maintenance on 6th Street and High Street waterline
edwardsville/1.summary: High Street residents asked about the 2027 waterline and street sealing, and complained about dust on unmaintained 6th Street.

edwardsville/2.title: Interim city manager and staff pay study
edwardsville/2.summary: The council approved Doug Gerber as interim city manager and hired Salary.com for a compensation study after staff losses.

edwardsville/3.title: Flex business park PUD and Kaw Drive development
edwardsville/3.summary: The planning commission held a hearing on Elevated Ventures Group's flex-use business park and reviewed a development plan and special use permit on Kaw Drive.

edwardsville/4.title: Housing allowed at 725 S Ford Street
edwardsville/4.summary: A resident raised the zoning and allowed housing types for a property on South Ford Street.

edwardsville/5.title: Richland Avenue and 106th Street road work
edwardsville/5.summary: The mayor asked for an update on Richland Avenue and 106th Street improvements and a postcard to homeowners before closing out the project; a resident praised the new 104th Street sidewalk.

edwardsville/6.title: River Front Park clearing and Veterans Monument
edwardsville/6.summary: The parks board discussed clearing trees along River Front Park and the trail, a new playground, and a Veterans Monument; the council later awarded a $58,500 tree clearing contract.

edwardsville/7.title: Dangerous house at 609 Newton Street
edwardsville/7.summary: The council set a public hearing on the condition of the residential structure at 609 Newton Street.

fairway/0.title: Flooding on Brookridge Drive
fairway/0.summary: The council hired Water Resource Solutions for a preliminary study of flooding on Brookridge Drive, aiming for county stormwater (SMAC) cost sharing.

fairway/1.title: Speeding on Mission Road
fairway/1.summary: The city reported recent complaints about speeding on Mission Road.

fairway/2.title: Sidewalk on 53rd Street through an improvement district
fairway/2.summary: A committee is considering creating a benefit district to pay for a sidewalk along 53rd Street.

fairway/3.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral rate
fairway/3.summary: Fairway held hearings on exceeding the revenue-neutral rate and adopting its 2027 budget after reviewing sales tax and cash flow.

fairway/4.title: Feature tree removal, fences and home site plans
fairway/4.summary: The council and planning commission reviewed a protected feature tree removal at 5501 Falmouth Road and exceptions for greenspace and corner-lot fences on Eastvale, Alhambra and El Monte.
fairway/4.where: 5501 Falmouth Rd; Eastvale Dr; Alhambra St; El Monte St

fairway/5.title: Solar panel rules and stormwater basin upkeep
fairway/5.summary: The planning commission discussed solar regulations and maintenance of stormwater retention basins in residential areas.

gardner/0.title: Flock license plate cameras
gardner/0.summary: Residents repeatedly asked the council not to renew the city's Flock camera contract, citing tracking of people's movements and misuse elsewhere; the police chief described the one stationary camera and policies.

gardner/1.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral rate
gardner/1.summary: Gardner adopted a 17.814 mill levy above the 16.933 revenue-neutral rate after several residents objected to rising costs and utility bills; two councilmembers voted no.

gardner/2.title: Project Velocity incentives
gardner/2.summary: The council approved a non-binding agreement for Project Velocity, a development that includes a performing arts and education building and seeks a mix of tax incentives; a resident questioned the incentives and construction traffic near Walmart.

gardner/3.title: 215-acre development at I-35 and 175th Street
gardner/3.summary: The council rezoned about 215 acres between the railroad and I-35 near 175th Street for roughly 2.5 million square feet of development tied to a new 175th Street interchange; nearby residents spoke at hearings.

gardner/4.title: Eminent domain for 167th, 175th and Grand Street projects
gardner/4.summary: Gardner moved to condemn land for the 167th Street, 175th Street and Grand Street (Pine to Center) road projects after authorizing purchases.

gardner/5.title: Fireworks complaints
gardner/5.summary: Residents complained about loud fireworks outside allowed times and asked for fewer fireworks days, while others said rules were followed; council noted new signs helped.

gardner/6.title: Electric utility costs, substations and $56 million in bonds
gardner/6.summary: Tariffs raised the price of a Substation 4 transformer, a generator repair grew to $2.75 million, and the city scheduled about $56 million in bonds for electric work and the Hillsdale Lake water intake.

gardner/7.title: Kill Creek wastewater plant expansion
gardner/7.summary: The council approved the next construction phase of the Kill Creek Water Resource Recovery Facility expansion and amended bond authorizations for sewer, water and electric work.

gardner/8.title: Short-term rental at 633 Colleen
gardner/8.summary: A resident complained a home on Colleen was operating as an unpermitted Airbnb; the council later took up a conditional use permit for it.

gardner/9.title: Clare Crossing apartments and 167th and Clare annexation
gardner/9.summary: The council re-approved rezoning for the Clare Crossing apartments and commercial development and annexed about 70 acres at 167th Street and Clare Road.

gardner/10.title: Selling Gardner Lake
gardner/10.summary: A resident urged the council to keep Gardner Lake as a city asset instead of selling it.

gardner/11.title: City administrator departure
gardner/11.summary: The council approved a separation agreement with City Administrator James Pruetting and named Amy Nasta interim administrator.

gardner/12.title: Truck traffic on 188th Street at Vivian
gardner/12.summary: A church asked for signs warning semis that 188th Street at Vivian is not a through street after repeated trucks turning around in its lot.

lake-quivira/0.title: Zoning regulation updates
lake-quivira/0.summary: Residents commented on proposed zoning regulation updates after a joint work session, including a memo from two residents.

lake-quivira/1.title: Construction workers parking on roads
lake-quivira/1.summary: The building official proposed enforcement letters and fines from performance bonds for construction crews parking in ways that block traffic and emergency vehicles.

lake-quivira/2.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral rate
lake-quivira/2.summary: The council adopted a 2027 budget levying above the revenue-neutral rate with no public comment.

lake-quivira/3.title: Dam inspection, spillway and water level alarms
lake-quivira/3.summary: The city contracted the state for a dam inspection and updated contacts for its water level detection system.

lake-quivira/4.title: Trash contract and Holliday Drive cleanup
lake-quivira/4.summary: The council considered extending its Waste Management contract and a right-of-way cleanup along Holliday Drive and Renner Road.

leawood/0.title: Town Center Plaza redevelopment and a 1-cent shopping district sales tax
leawood/0.summary: Federal Realty presented a $59.8 million makeover of Leawood Town Center Plaza and Town Center Crossing and asked for a Community Improvement District adding a one-cent sales tax for up to 22 years to raise about $35.6 million.

leawood/1.title: March 2027 mail-ballot vote on a street and stormwater sales tax
leawood/1.summary: The council called a mail ballot election for March 2, 2027 on a new 1/8-cent city sales tax for ten years to fund streets, stormwater and public safety.

leawood/2.title: 2027 budget, capital plan and exceeding the revenue-neutral rate
leawood/2.summary: Leawood held public hearings on its 2027 budget, a 2027-2031 capital improvement program and a property tax rate above the revenue-neutral rate, and also revised council pay.

leawood/3.title: State Line Road access changes at 85th Terrace to 86th Terrace
leawood/3.summary: A study of cut-through traffic and crashes near State Line Road weighed turn restrictions and a median closure; residents on 85th Terrace, 86th Street and 86th Terrace split in a survey and spoke at committee.
leawood/3.where: State Line Rd, 85th Ter to 86th Ter

leawood/4.title: Indian Creek floodplain plan and a berm near Leawood City Park
leawood/4.summary: The stormwater committee reviewed an Indian Creek floodplain master plan from Mission Road to State Line, including a berm near Mission Road and I-435 and fill around City Park; possible buyouts are unfunded.
leawood/4.where: Indian Creek, Mission Rd to State Line Rd

leawood/5.title: Rooted and Reaching comprehensive plan and the future of 135th Street
leawood/5.summary: Leaders worked through the draft comprehensive plan's open questions, including redevelopment, housing choice and the long-term vision for the 135th Street corridor; planners also discussed loosening mixed-use ratios.

leawood/6.title: Safe Streets Leawood (Vision Zero) plan
leawood/6.summary: A federally funded safety plan presented crash data, resident requests for traffic calming and speed enforcement, and proposed fixes like protected left turns and curb extensions.

leawood/7.title: New townhomes and brownstones near 133rd-135th Streets
leawood/7.summary: The council approved plans for Leawood Market Center Townhomes and Village East Brownstones near 135th Street.

leawood/8.title: Sidewalks in the 2027 residential street rebuilds
leawood/8.summary: Staff presented plans to add sidewalks as part of the 2027 residential reconstruction program.

leawood/9.title: Sign rules for construction and temporary signs
leawood/9.summary: The planning commission held hearings on development ordinance amendments for temporary signs and signs during construction, later adopted by the council.

leawood/10.title: Public art along Tomahawk Creek Parkway (Art Line Leawood)
leawood/10.summary: The public art committee named the Tomahawk Creek Parkway collection Art Line Leawood and revised sites in the public art master plan.

sources.body: Arts in Public Places Initiative [APPI] (Sub-committee of the Leawood Arts Council)

lenexa/0.title: WaterOne mine remediation at 10401 Renner Boulevard
lenexa/0.summary: WaterOne sought a rezoning and five-year special use permit to run a mining and quarrying operation at 10401 Renner Boulevard to remediate an old mine, with a public hearing at the planning commission before council approval.

lenexa/1.title: Tax breaks for Lenexa Logistics Centre North warehouses
lenexa/1.summary: The council moved forward with about $42.5 million and $20 million in industrial revenue bonds and tax abatements for large Lenexa Logistics Centre North Phase II warehouse buildings, plus a special benefit district for Britton Street.

lenexa/2.title: City Center parking study
lenexa/2.summary: As City Center gets busier, the council hired Kimley-Horn to study parking and curb use and recommend parking management and new parking.
lenexa/2.where: Lenexa City Center (87th St Pkwy & Renner)

lenexa/3.title: Seven Hills Lake stormwater project
lenexa/3.summary: The council combined two phases of the Seven Hills Lake stormwater improvements into one capital project.

lenexa/4.title: 83rd Street rebuild from Gleason to Clare Road
lenexa/4.summary: Road widening on 83rd Street requires relocating septic systems for three affected homes.
lenexa/4.where: 83rd St, Gleason Rd to Clare Rd

lenexa/5.title: Little Mill Creek Park and Cottonwood Street rebuild
lenexa/5.summary: Final design was approved to rebuild Cottonwood Street in concrete and add parking at Little Mill Creek Park and the Municipal Services Center.
lenexa/5.where: Little Mill Creek Park / Cottonwood St

lenexa/6.title: Neighborhood Beautification Grant pilot
lenexa/6.summary: Lenexa created a $20,000 pilot program giving neighborhoods matching grants of up to $2,000 for visible improvements.

lenexa/7.title: St. James Academy additions on Prairie Star Parkway
lenexa/7.summary: Planners and the council reviewed about 46,000 square feet of additions and more parking at St. James Academy.

lenexa/8.title: Sikh Gurudwara parking expansion on Marion Street
lenexa/8.summary: A request to expand parking and add a maintenance building at the Midwest Sikh Gurudwara in a single-family district was continued to November.

lenexa/9.title: Shops at Vista Village and Westchester Square
lenexa/9.summary: Planners approved new multitenant commercial buildings at Prairie Star Parkway and Ridgeview and on 101st Street, and a facade refresh at Westchester Square at 87th and Pflumm.
lenexa/9.where: Prairie Star Pkwy & Ridgeview Rd; 87th St & Pflumm Rd

lenexa/10.title: 99th Street and Woodsonia Drive special assessments
lenexa/10.summary: The council levied special assessments to pay for up to $10.6 million in public improvements in the 99th and Woodsonia benefit district.

lenexa/11.title: Strang Line Road streetlights
lenexa/11.summary: Lenexa awarded a $484,000 contract for new streetlights and stormwater work on Strang Line Road south of College Boulevard.
lenexa/11.where: Strang Line Rd south of College Blvd

lenexa/12.title: Meritex underground data center expansion at 99th and Britton
lenexa/12.summary: The council approved a 30-acre Meritex business park whose first building will hold chillers and standby generators for Lightedge, a colocation data center in the Meritex underground; councilmembers asked about noise, generator emissions and whether it counts as a data center.

merriam/0.title: Downtown Master Plan, Turkey Creek flooding and building scale
merriam/0.summary: Merriam's downtown plan weighed three visions for how much to build, with a 471-response survey showing 49% support for downtown housing; the Turkey Creek floodplain, creek ownership and costly flood control dominate the debate, and a resident criticized the cost estimates.
merriam/0.where: Downtown Merriam / Merriam Dr & Turkey Creek

merriam/1.title: Possible downtown sales tax ballot question
merriam/1.summary: After survey respondents favored a quarter-cent sales tax for downtown improvements, the council discussed putting a downtown sales tax on the ballot.

merriam/2.title: 1% for Art ordinance on new development
merriam/2.summary: Council worked on an ordinance requiring commercial and apartment projects over $1 million to install public art or pay into a public art fund, with affordable housing exempt.

merriam/3.title: New public art at the Butterfly Garden
merriam/3.summary: The public art committee picked finalists and heard artist presentations for a new piece near the Butterfly Garden, and discussed future sites like Brown Park and a long-sought bridge over Shawnee Mission Parkway.

merriam/4.title: IKEA parking garage removal
merriam/4.summary: Planners reviewed IKEA's request to tear down its aging 65,000 square foot parking structure at 6000 IKEA Way.

merriam/5.title: Massage therapy licensing rules
merriam/5.summary: The council amended city rules on massage therapy businesses over two readings.

merriam/6.title: Shawnee Creek channel work and capital plan
merriam/6.summary: Merriam hired Olsson to design the Shawnee Creek channel project, and planners found the 2026-2031 capital improvement plan consistent with the comprehensive plan.

merriam/7.title: Adopting 2024 fire and building codes
merriam/7.summary: The council considered ordinances adopting the 2024 international fire and building codes.

mission-hills/0.title: Cell tower leases and a possible new tower at City Hall
mission-hills/0.summary: After T-Mobile sent notice cancelling its lease at 6400 State Line Road and asked for a 130-150 foot monopole, the council began weighing options, including a site in the trees on the City Hall grounds along Tomahawk Road, ahead of a February 2027 AT&T lease deadline.

mission-hills/1.title: Speeding on 67th Street and golf carts on city streets
mission-hills/1.summary: A resident reported drivers going about 70 mph on 67th Street west of Belinder; police described enforcement details and discussed residents driving golf carts that may not be street legal.

mission-hills/2.title: License plate reader cameras and data retention
mission-hills/2.summary: Prairie Village police, who patrol Mission Hills, answered resident questions about license plate readers, including the 90-day retention period, who can search the data and audits.

mission-hills/3.title: 2027 budget and rising property taxes
mission-hills/3.summary: At the budget hearing a resident said his property taxes have grown more than 6% a year since 2020, and officials explained the county appraiser's role and rising costs.

mission-hills/4.title: Eisenhower Pond watershed and 2027-2028 street and stormwater work
mission-hills/4.summary: The council adopted a 2027-2031 capital plan and reviewed a concept study for street and stormwater projects in the Eisenhower Pond watershed, plus work on Belinder south of 69th and 70th Terrace.
mission-hills/4.where: Belinder Ave south of 69th St; 70th Ter

mission-hills/5.title: Fireworks ordinance
mission-hills/5.summary: A city committee took up possible changes to the fireworks ordinance.

mission-hills/6.title: Pet license rules
mission-hills/6.summary: The council discussed changes to the pet license ordinance and tagging process.

mission-hills/7.title: Indian Hills Country Club driving range net along 69th Street
mission-hills/7.summary: The architectural review board considered a protective net fence with seventeen tall poles along the 69th Street side of the club's driving range.
mission-hills/7.where: 69th St at Indian Hills Country Club

mission/0.title: 647 apartments at Foxridge and Broadmoor
mission/0.summary: Block Real Estate proposed three apartment buildings totaling 647 units at 5665 Foxridge and 5700 Broadmoor, including converting an office building; the council voted 9-0 to send it back to the planning commission over traffic, exterior materials and feasibility, and it returned in October.

mission/1.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral property tax rate
mission/1.summary: Mission held hearings on its 2027 budget and the Rock Creek drainage district budgets, with resolutions to levy above the revenue-neutral rate.

mission/2.title: 2027 trash and stormwater utility fees
mission/2.summary: The council set 2027 solid waste and stormwater utility rates, with stormwater at $28 per residential unit per month, billed on property tax statements.

mission/3.title: Rock Creek and neighborhood stormwater projects
mission/3.summary: The city approved Evergy utility relocation for the Rock Creek project, changed the scope of localized stormwater design, and ordered design of 2027 street and stormwater projects.

mission/4.title: Complete Streets policy
mission/4.summary: Staff presented a draft Complete Streets policy so future street projects serve people walking, biking and riding transit as well as drivers.

olathe/0.title: Rock quarry permits near 151st Street and Old 56 Highway
olathe/0.summary: Aggregate companies asked to rezone about 109 acres and get special use permits for new and expanded rock quarries southeast of 151st and Old 56 Highway/Clare Road. The council also met in closed session about the pending quarry applications.

olathe/1.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral property tax rate
olathe/1.summary: Olathe held a public hearing on its FY2027 budget and its intent to exceed the revenue-neutral rate. Residents spoke about rising taxes and household costs, and the council discussed growth-driven service needs and a $300,000 property-tax rebate program.

olathe/2.title: FTI manufacturing campus and tax breaks at 167th and Lone Elm
olathe/2.summary: Faith Technologies' 120-plus acre manufacturing campus got site plans and plats approved, along with industrial revenue bonds and property-tax phase-ins for about 1.5 million square feet of buildings.

olathe/3.title: New logistics warehouses along 167th to 175th Streets
olathe/3.summary: Developers sought rezonings for the 167th Street Logistics Centre (51 acres) and Frontier Trails Logistics (70 acres of general industrial near 175th), and revised plans for Great Plains Commerce Center buildings.

olathe/4.title: College and Sunnybrook apartments and shopping
olathe/4.summary: The council rezoned business-park land at College Boulevard and Sunnybrook for a commercial center and 333 rental apartments, debating whether it delivers the mixed use the comprehensive plan calls for.

olathe/5.title: Residences at Heritage Park apartments near 151st/159th and Pflumm
olathe/5.summary: Rodrock Development asked to rezone about 25 acres to medium-density multifamily for the Residences at Heritage Park; the hearing was continued once before returning in October.

olathe/6.title: Rewrite of Olathe's development code and housing affordability
olathe/6.summary: Council debated a contract to rewrite the Unified Development Ordinance over 18 months, discussing housing affordability and a wider variety of housing types.

olathe/7.title: Fire station replacement and repairs
olathe/7.summary: Olathe approved construction of the Fire Station No. 4 replacement on Mur-Len Road and a critical remediation project at Fire Station No. 1.

olathe/8.title: Santa Fe Street widening from Ridgeview to Mur-Len
olathe/8.summary: Council reviewed the Santa Fe Street improvements project and related utility agreements, plus a K-10 and Lone Elm bypass design contract.
olathe/8.where: Santa Fe St, Ridgeview to Mur-Len

olathe/9.title: Parkside Reserve and other new subdivisions in south Olathe
olathe/9.summary: Final plats added nearly 90 new lots at Parkside Reserve near 167th and Black Bob, plus Stonebridge Manor and Woodland Hills phases.

overland-park/0.title: Proposed 1/4-cent sales tax for parks (Playbook OP)
overland-park/0.summary: After adopting the Playbook OP parks plan, which has a $248 million funding gap, the Committee of the Whole chose to ask voters for a dedicated 1/4-cent parks and recreation sales tax. Ballot language comes back November 2.

overland-park/1.title: Black & Veatch headquarters and Overland Park Plaza II redevelopment
overland-park/1.summary: The council approved TIF and community improvement district financing for Black & Veatch's new 729,000-square-foot headquarters near 112th–115th and Nall, the first phase of a plan that could add 700 apartments, a hotel and more offices.

sources.body: Finance, Administration and Economic Development Committee
Finance, Administration and Economic Development Committee

overland-park/2.title: 2027 budget exceeding the revenue-neutral rate
overland-park/2.summary: Overland Park held its hearing and approved a property tax rate above the revenue-neutral rate with the 2027 budget, while promoting a second round of its property tax rebate program.

sources.body: Finance, Administration and Economic Development Committee

overland-park/3.title: Citywide organized trash and recycling collection
overland-park/3.summary: The council held a public hearing and adopted a resolution of intent to move to an organized, city-contracted collection service for residential trash, recycling and yard waste.

overland-park/4.title: Oak Park Mall rezoning to mixed use
overland-park/4.summary: Mall owner CBL Properties asked to rezone parts of Oak Park Mall at 95th and Quivira to general business and mixed use to allow changes to the mall; the planning commission received public comment on the revised plan.

overland-park/5.title: Brookridge redevelopment and I-435 mixed-use rezoning
overland-park/5.summary: The former Brookridge golf course site near 103rd and Antioch is seeking mixed-use rezoning, and its developer gave a project update and assigned TIF/CID proceeds to its lender.

sources.body: Finance, Administration and Economic Development Committee

overland-park/6.title: The Woods mixed-use development at US-69 and I-435
overland-park/6.summary: A rezoning to mixed use was requested for The Woods at the southeast corner of US-69 and I-435.

overland-park/7.title: Metcalf corridor TIF districts (8036 and 8201 Metcalf)
overland-park/7.summary: The council approved TIF and CID financing for a redevelopment at 8036 Metcalf (80th Street) after a public hearing, and the planning commission reviewed a TIF plan for 8201 Metcalf.

overland-park/8.title: 167th Street and US-69 rezoning for homes, apartments and shops
overland-park/8.summary: A large rezoning at the southwest corner of 167th and US-69 would allow single-family homes, high-rise apartments and commercial uses; it required a public hearing and was continued.

overland-park/9.title: Antioch Homes apartments at 7235 Antioch
overland-park/9.summary: Gravel Development asked to rezone 7235 Antioch Road to garden apartments for multifamily housing.

overland-park/10.title: Development code rewrite, including rules for new single-family homes
overland-park/10.summary: Staff presented Unified Development Ordinance updates, including new standards for single-family construction, and neighborhood groups were briefed.

overland-park/11.title: Police license plate reader cameras
overland-park/11.summary: The police department briefed the public safety committee on its automated license plate readers, including access to cameras run by private businesses.

overland-park/12.title: Bike and pedestrian network (Active Mobility Plan) and e-bike safety
overland-park/12.summary: Staff kicked off an Active Mobility Plan to connect trails, sidewalks and bike routes, while the environmental council discussed e-bikes and bike safety.

overland-park/13.title: Storm sewer and drainage repairs
overland-park/13.summary: Contracts were approved for 2025–2027 storm drainage and major storm sewer repair projects, including the Bluejacket line.

overland-park/14.title: Downtown restorations (Dream Theatre at the Rio, Strang Depot)
overland-park/14.summary: The city moved toward funding the reopening of the Dream Theatre at the Rio and approved more aid for restoring the former Strang Depot at 80th and Santa Fe.

sources.body: Finance, Administration and Economic Development Committee

overland-park/15.title: New subdivisions in south Overland Park
overland-park/15.summary: Plats were approved for Sundance Ridge neighborhoods near 175th and State Line, Falls at Wolf Creek, Southern Meadows and Prairie Wolf Flats.

prairie-village/0.title: Amending the conversion therapy ban
prairie-village/0.summary: The council revisited its ban on conversion therapy for minors, debating First Amendment concerns and proposed amendments; residents spoke on both sides and a committee vote split 7-4.

prairie-village/1.title: E-bike and e-scooter rules and a first-responder "halo law"
prairie-village/1.summary: Proposed ordinance amendments would regulate e-bikes and e-scooters and create a buffer zone around first responders; residents asked the council to postpone and gather more input.

prairie-village/2.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral property tax rate
prairie-village/2.summary: Prairie Village held hearings on its 2027 budget and its intent to levy above the revenue-neutral rate.

prairie-village/3.title: Brush Creek wastewater pump station rebuild at Porter Park
prairie-village/3.summary: Johnson County Wastewater plans to rebuild the Brush Creek pump station, and the city considered easements and park impacts at Porter Park.

prairie-village/4.title: 83rd Street rebuild from Mission Road to Nall
prairie-village/4.summary: The city planned improvements to 83rd Street between Mission Road and Nall Avenue, with residents raising traffic speed concerns.
prairie-village/4.where: 83rd St, Mission Rd to Nall Ave

prairie-village/5.title: Responding to the state by-right housing law (SB 418)
prairie-village/5.summary: Planning staff briefed officials on how the new state law allowing certain housing by right affects Prairie Village zoning.

prairie-village/6.title: Chemical-free parks and a Monarch waystation
prairie-village/6.summary: Residents and the parks committee discussed reducing pesticide use in parks and adding pollinator habitat.

prairie-village/7.title: Public Art Master Plan
prairie-village/7.summary: The arts council presented and the council considered a citywide public art master plan.

prairie-village/8.title: Johnson County Library agreement
prairie-village/8.summary: The council considered a memorandum of understanding with the Johnson County Library on the Corinth branch.

prairie-village/9.title: Purchasing policy changes
prairie-village/9.summary: The council updated its purchasing policy and spending thresholds.

prairie-village/10.title: Trash and recycling contract with GFL
prairie-village/10.summary: The city considered its solid waste contract with GFL Environmental.

prairie-village/11.title: Consolidated Fire District No. 2 budget
prairie-village/11.summary: Officials reviewed the fire district's budget and its effect on the city.

shawnee/0.title: Fireworks rules after the Fourth of July
shawnee/0.summary: After a committee discussion of complaints about fireworks, a vendor and residents spoke at council asking for changes such as stronger enforcement instead of new limits on Fourth of July fireworks use.

shawnee/1.title: Midland Entertainment District TIF and area plan
shawnee/1.summary: With a tax increment financing district already in place near I-435 and Midland Drive, staff proposed a $150,000 area plan to guide redevelopment of stalled parcels and direct TIF money.

shawnee/2.title: Overlook at Midland apartments
shawnee/2.summary: The planning commission held a public hearing on a planned unit development for multifamily housing just south of Shawnee Mission Parkway near Midland Drive.

shawnee/3.title: $18 million police Justice Center expansion
shawnee/3.summary: The council considered an $18 million budget and design-build contracts to expand the Shawnee Police Department's Justice Center.

shawnee/4.title: Johnson Drive intersection rebuilds at Barker, Quivira and I-435
shawnee/4.summary: Shawnee awarded a $1.75 million contract for the Johnson Drive and Barker Road intersection with added federal safety money, replaced the old Johnson Drive and Quivira signal, and hired engineers for the I-435 interchange.
shawnee/4.where: Johnson Dr at Barker Rd, Quivira Rd and I-435

shawnee/5.title: Hands-free driving ordinance
shawnee/5.summary: Police and the city attorney proposed widening the ban on using phones while driving to cover apps, video, social media and browsing.

shawnee/6.title: Annual offense code update, license plate covers and animal cruelty
shawnee/6.summary: The council adopted the 2026 Uniform Public Offense Code with local amendments on license plate covers, animal cruelty rules for community cats, and keeping distance from officers.

shawnee/7.title: 57th and Barton townhomes downtown
shawnee/7.summary: Planners reviewed a 10-unit townhome building at 57th Street and Barton Drive in the downtown mixed-use area.

shawnee/8.title: Sewer extensions and new subdivisions in western Shawnee
shawnee/8.summary: The council expanded the county sewer district for Heartland Logistics Park, Mill Creek Road, Mize Road and Woodland Drive sites and approved plats like Canyon Lakes Eighth and Good Deeds Ranch.
shawnee/8.where: Western Shawnee (Clare Rd, Mize Rd, 63rd St)

shawnee/9.title: Community Development Block Grant 2027 plan
shawnee/9.summary: Public hearings were held on how Shawnee will spend its 2027 federal CDBG money.

spring-hill/0.title: New wastewater treatment plant and sewer rates
spring-hill/0.summary: With the current plant expected to hit capacity in three years, Spring Hill held a public hearing on a facilities plan for a new plant near Ten Mile and Sweetwater Creeks and its impact on ratepayers, then moved ahead with design and bonds.

spring-hill/1.title: Storm shelter requirement for new homes
spring-hill/1.summary: The city considered requiring storm protection in new houses and townhomes; a resident supported it and a homebuilder spoke against it.

spring-hill/2.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral rate
spring-hill/2.summary: Spring Hill held two hearings and adopted a 2027 mill levy above the revenue-neutral rate.

spring-hill/3.title: Comprehensive plan update and future land use near 191st-199th Streets
spring-hill/3.summary: The city kicked off a comprehensive plan update with open houses and pop-ups; a resident asked that land around homes near Renner and Lackman along 191st and 199th Streets be planned to protect them.

spring-hill/4.title: Making development review more open to the public
spring-hill/4.summary: Council discussed better access to records and development applications, notifying nearby owners before hearings and more ways for residents to weigh in.

spring-hill/5.title: Rezonings at 183rd and Woodland and on Madison Street
spring-hill/5.summary: Neighbors raised environmental and site concerns about a rezoning to single-family lots at 183rd Street and Woodland Road, approved alongside a commercial-to-industrial rezoning at 19072 Madison (Bucyrus Auto).

spring-hill/6.title: Ozark Ready Mix plant on Webster Street
spring-hill/6.summary: Planners held hearings on rezoning and a conditional use permit amendment for Ozark Ready Mix at 18430 Webster Street.

spring-hill/7.title: Flooding and stormwater runoff complaints
spring-hill/7.summary: Residents on 207th Street and Parker Street described flooding and runoff from nearby development and asked for a review of the site's stormwater plan, as the city adopted a state-required stormwater program.

spring-hill/8.title: Fireworks and door-to-door solicitors
spring-hill/8.summary: Residents asked to limit fireworks dates and locations and raised concerns about solicitors; free "No Soliciting" stickers were offered at City Hall.

spring-hill/9.title: Road grants and Vision Zero
spring-hill/9.summary: The city sought KDOT grants for K-7/US-169 signal timing, a 223rd Street roundabout, a 183rd Street signal and South Street sidewalks, and adopted a Vision Zero safety policy.

spring-hill/10.title: Planning commission membership rules
spring-hill/10.summary: Amendments to planning commission and zoning appeals rules covered attendance-based removal and appointing non-residents.

unified-government/0.title: Countywide sales tax on the November ballot for homelessness services
unified-government/0.summary: The Commission put a special-purpose countywide sales tax on the November 3 ballot tied to services for the unhoused population, and discussed creating a citizen oversight board for how the money is spent.

sources.body: Planning & Zoning and Board of Commission
Planning & Zoning and Board of Commission

unified-government/1.title: 2027 budget and exceeding the revenue-neutral rate
unified-government/1.summary: After weeks of department budget workshops, the UG held a hearing on its amended 2026 and proposed 2027 budgets and its intent to exceed the revenue-neutral rate. Commissioners pushed to drop an extra mill from the proposed levy.

sources.body: Planning & Zoning and Board of Commission

unified-government/2.title: Late-August storm recovery and debris cleanup
unified-government/2.summary: The Commission extended the storm emergency declaration, heard updates on state assistance, SBA disaster loans and debris removal, and got regular cleanup reports into October.

sources.body: Planning & Zoning and Board of Commission

unified-government/3.title: Midtown Station development and its feasibility study
unified-government/3.summary: The proposed Midtown Station project was sent back to committee, and commissioners required an independent financial feasibility and economic impact study before voting.

unified-government/4.title: Short-term rental permits and neighbor complaints
unified-government/4.summary: Many non-owner-occupied short-term rentals came up for special use permits and renewals. Commissioners debated being notified of complaints and police reports, and an appeal tested the renewal rules.

sources.body: Planning & Zoning and Board of Commission

unified-government/5.title: State "by-right" housing law and accessory dwelling units
unified-government/5.summary: Planners presented changes required by Kansas's new By-Right Housing Development Act (SB 418), and the Commission advanced an ordinance allowing accessory dwelling units.

unified-government/6.title: Demolishing the old downtown library at 625 Minnesota Avenue
unified-government/6.summary: The Landmarks Commission voted down permission to demolish the former library in the Downtown Commercial Historic District, and the decision went on to the Commission.

sources.body: Planning & Zoning and Board of Commission

unified-government/7.title: Liquor store proposed near a church at 4732 State Avenue
unified-government/7.summary: An applicant sought a variance and special use permit for a liquor store about 1,180 feet from Grace Temple Baptist Church, inside the 1,300-foot buffer the code requires.

unified-government/8.title: Police surveillance technology and new officers
unified-government/8.summary: KCKPD updated commissioners on its real-time crime center, license plate readers and drones, and accepted a federal COPS grant to hire 12 more patrol officers.

unified-government/9.title: Restructuring the Wyandotte County Library Board
unified-government/9.summary: A charter resolution abolished and recreated the countywide library board with fewer members, and the new board drafted bylaws for splitting library levy money.

unified-government/10.title: Land Bank homes and new housing in northeast KCK
unified-government/10.summary: The Land Bank reported 478 active option agreements, and the CJR project north of Quindaro, expected to bring 400 to 500 homes, has started pulling building permits.

unified-government/11.title: STAR bonds and the Kaw River bridge financing
unified-government/11.summary: The Commission amended its STAR bond participation ordinance for a major sports project and changed how CID money on the Kaw River bridge development repays costs.

unified-government/12.title: Community Benefit Ordinance spending (parks, home child care, housing trust)
unified-government/12.summary: The advisory board reviewed how Village West-area community benefit money funds parks projects, home-based child care grants and a housing trust fund, and recommended 2026 allocations.

sources.body: Planning & Zoning and Board of Commission

unified-government/13.title: American Royal fee spending on fiber and a downtown plan
unified-government/13.summary: Leftover American Royal fee money ($1.47 million) was allocated to fiber expansion along Leavenworth Road, Parallel and Fairfax and a mini master plan for downtown KCK.

unified-government/14.title: Downtown KCK improvement district renewal
unified-government/14.summary: The downtown self-supported municipal improvement district was found consistent with the comprehensive plan and re-established, funding crosswalks and "KCK Letters" projects.

sources.body: Planning & Zoning and Board of Commission

unified-government/15.title: Park upgrades for the World Cup and a new golf clubhouse
unified-government/15.summary: The parks capital plan includes paving and lighting at Wyandotte County Park, Kaw Point and other sites ahead of the World Cup, and the park board pushed a $9.5 million golf clubhouse.
